query: Which robustness methods should be primary versus secondary: staggered-DiD (CS/SA), synthetic control/matrix completion, doubly-robust DiD, Lee/Manski bounds, and leave-one-out diagnostics?

response.query: Which robustness methods should be primary versus secondary: staggered-DiD (CS/SA), synthetic control/matrix completion, doubly-robust DiD, Lee/Manski bounds, and leave-one-out diagnostics?
response.answer: Doubly-robust DiD and synthetic control should be primary; staggered-DiD, matrix completion, and leave-one-out diagnostics secondary.

results.title: Notes on Callaway & Sant’Anna (2021) – Staggered Adoption DiD | Chen Xing
results.content: + Define $G$ as the time period when a unit **first becomes treated**. + $Y\_{it}(g)$: outcome at time $t$ if first treated in period $g$. Why focus on time after treatment starting period, $t \ge g$? Given that we never observe $Y(\infty)$ in post-treatment periods among units that have been treated, we need to make assumptions to identify $\operatorname{ATT}(g, t)$. Under no anticipation and one of the parallel-trends assumptions, each $\mathrm{ATT}(g,t)$ equals a simple **long-difference DID**:. For each treated cohort, the method computes the difference in outcomes between the pre-treatment period and a specific post-treatment period, potentially far apart in time. With unconfoundedness holding, we can then apply **standard treatment effects estimators**, including **doubly robust methods** and matching, utilizing **all not-yet-treated units** as the valid control group for that specific cross-section. library(readstata13) library(readstata13) library(readstata13)library(ggplot2) library(ggplot2) library(ggplot2)library(did) # Callaway & Sant'Anna library(did) # Callaway & Sant'Anna library(did) # Callaway & Sant'Anna castle <- data.frame(read.dta13('')) castle <- data.frame(read.dta13('')) castle<-data.frame(read.dta13(''))castle$effyear[is.na(castle$effyear)] <- 0 # untreated units have effective year of 0 castle$effyear[is.na(castle$effyear)] <- 0 # untreated units have effective year of 0 castle $ effyear[is.na(castle $ effyear)]<- 0 # untreated units have effective year of 0 # Estimating the effect on log(homicide) # Estimating the effect on log(homicide) # Estimating the effect on log(homicide)atts <- att_gt(yname = "l_homicide", # LHS variable atts <- att_gt(yname = "l_homicide", # LHS variable atts<- att_gt(yname = "l_homicide", # LHS variable tname = "year", # time variable tname = "year", # time variable tname = "year", # time variable idname = "sid", # id variable idname = "sid", # id variable idname = "sid", # id variable gname = "effyear", # first treatment period variable gname = "effyear", # first treatment period variable gname = "effyear", # first treatment period variable data = castle, # data data = castle, # data data = castle, # data xformla = NULL, # no covariates xformla = NULL, # no covariates xformla = NULL, # no covariates #xformla = ~ l_police, # with covariates #xformla = ~ l_police, # with covariates #xformla = ~ l_police, # with covariates est_method = "dr", # "dr" is doubly robust.
